skill.name: azure-resource-lookup
skill.description: Find and summarize Azure resources across subscriptions and resource groups using Azure Resource Graph, Azure CLI, and Azure MCP tools. It supports inventory, tag audits, orphaned resource discovery, and read-only resource lookup.
skill.summary: Read-only Azure resource discovery with Resource Graph and MCP routing.
skill.author: microsoft

content.value_statement: Azure teams need quick inventory answers across subscriptions. This skill uses Azure Resource Graph patterns to list, filter, and summarize resources.
actual_capabilities: Lists Azure resources by type, subscription, or resource group using Azure Resource Graph.
Generates Azure Resource Graph query commands from natural language requests.
Routes common resource types to dedicated Azure MCP tools when coverage is better.
Identifies orphaned resources such as unattached disks, unused public IPs, and idle load balancers.
Supports tag, compliance, health, and provisioning state checks with KQL patterns.
Formats query results with JMESPath and table output guidance.
limitations: Does not deploy, create, update, or delete Azure resources.
Requires Azure CLI or MCP access with read permissions for selected subscriptions.
Azure Resource Graph data can have delay and is not suitable for real-time monitoring.
Query quality depends on accurate resource type names and subscription scope.

use_cases.title: Build a cloud inventory
use_cases.description: List resources across subscriptions and group results by type, location, or resource group.

use_cases.title: Check governance tags
use_cases.description: Find resources missing required tags and review tag coverage by service type.

use_cases.title: Find cleanup candidates
use_cases.description: Identify unattached disks, unused public IP addresses, and idle load balancers before cleanup review.

prompt_templates.title: List virtual machines
prompt_templates.prompt: List all virtual machines I can access. Show name, resource group, location, and power state.

prompt_templates.title: Find resources in a group
prompt_templates.prompt: Show every Azure resource in resource group <resource-group-name>. Include type, location, and subscription.

prompt_templates.title: Audit required tags
prompt_templates.prompt: Find resources that are missing Environment or CostCenter tags. Group the results by resource type.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect risky exposure signals
prompt_templates.prompt: Across subscriptions <subscription-ids>, find resources with public network access or failed provisioning. Limit results to the first 100 resources.

output_examples.input: Find unattached managed disks in my production subscription.
output: Found 3 unattached managed disks in the selected subscription.
Results include disk name, resource group, location, size, and SKU for ownership review.
Confirm business ownership before cleanup or deletion in another workflow.

output_examples.input: Show resources missing the CostCenter tag.
output: Found resources missing the CostCenter tag across compute, storage, and web service types.
The response groups results by resource type and includes resource group and subscription context.

output_examples.input: What App Services do I have in East US?
output: Returned App Service names, resource groups, locations, service plan identifiers, and current states.
The lookup is scoped to East US and uses Azure Resource Graph for services without full MCP coverage.

best_practices: Scope every lookup to known subscriptions or resource groups when possible.
Review generated Azure CLI commands before execution in shared or production tenants.
Limit large queries and request only the columns needed for the task.
anti_patterns: Using this skill to create, update, or delete Azure resources.
Running broad tenant inventory when a specific subscription or resource group is known.
Treating Azure Resource Graph results as live monitoring data.

faq.question: Can this skill change Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for read-only lookup, inventory, and discovery workflows.

faq.question: What access do I need?
faq.answer: You need Azure CLI or MCP access with read permissions for the subscriptions you want to query.

faq.question: Does it work across subscriptions?
faq.answer: Yes. It can query across subscriptions when the account has access and the query is scoped correctly.

faq.question: When should I use dedicated MCP tools instead?
faq.answer: Use dedicated tools for supported single-resource lookups when they provide fuller details than Resource Graph.

faq.question: Can it find orphaned resources?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for unattached disks, unused public IP addresses, orphaned NICs, and idle load balancers.

faq.question: Is Azure Resource Graph real time?
faq.answer: No. Results are near real time and can lag, so do not use it for active monitoring.
